fields.position: Clusters constrain candidates before OPQ coarse ranking and feature-aware FFN ranking over atomic documents. Fixed clusters/codebooks can mount fresh documents without sequential SID-prefix decoding.
fields.tradeoff: Cluster selection can still miss documents. Exact lookup proves a distance identity for existing quantized vectors, not better trained representations or production quality. A local snapshot is not a distributed atomic refresh.

fields.title: A cluster constrains candidates instead of assigning a unique semantic path
fields.body: WeSearch retains atomic documents inside a cluster union and separates coarse ranking from feature-aware ranking. MIMA instead lets multiple user interests propose candidates. Both require a fixed final deduplicated budget when comparing coverage; collecting more candidates does not establish better representations. The ADC identity verifies computation for one quantized representation, and fixed-artifact mounting does not replace training or coordinated model/index refresh.

fields.summary: Added WeSearch to distinguish cluster-constrained candidates, interest specialization, ADC distance equivalence and fixed-artifact mounting. L1 CPU evidence is not promoted to complete-retriever capability; production A/B and local mechanisms remain separate.
